claims.head: The Rangers will hunt a mismatch
claims.call: The Rangers’ L1 (Zibanejad, Lafrenière and Perreault) spends at least 39% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Zibanejad’s line (Zibanejad, Lafrenière and Perreault) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would. That’s Mike Sullivan chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Canucks’ third line is Boeser, O'Connor and Ohgren.
claims.nums: At home: 39% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 29% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Mike Sullivan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canucks’ third line.

claims.head: The Rangers come in rested
claims.body: It’s the Canucks’ second game in two nights, after last night in New Jersey. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Rangers get more of the play than usual.
claims.call: The Rangers get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.
claims.nums: Vancouver played yesterday · NY Rangers had a day off · NY Rangers’s usual share of 5-on-5 expected goals: 47.5%
claims.gist: The Canucks played last night; the Rangers are rested.

check.rule: held if the rested team's share of 5-on-5 expected goals is at or above its usual share; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Penalties could cost the Canucks
claims.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.5 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Rangers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Canucks more than most.
claims.nums: NY Rangers 5th for power play (8.5 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 32nd for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Rangers’ power play has a soft target in the Canucks’ kill.

NYR.head: The Rangers have nearly everything going for them
NYR.body: The Rangers have controlled the play far better over recent games, Vancouver is playing for the second night in a row, and the Rangers have home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Vancouver can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.

VAN.head: A steep climb for Vancouver
VAN.body: The Rangers have controlled the play far better over recent games, Vancouver is playing for the second night in a row, and the Rangers have home ice. Vancouver’s best hope is pouncing on loose pucks, plus a big night in goal.
